transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Samira Khan (Redwood Solutions), Maya Rodriguez (VeraHealth VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (VeraHealth Platform), Priya Sharma (VeraHealth Security)

Summary: Quick weekly POC sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider. Focus on latency (p50/p95), throughput, and tuning (batching, kv cache, quantization).

[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda - jordan will run through the numbers, then we cover ops questions and next steps
[00:15] Jordan: ok thanks, so as promised we compared the same prompt set and seq lengths vs the baseline provider you gave us. high level - p50 is roughly comparable, p95 we’re seeing a ~40-50% improvement on average with Redwood hosted config when kv cache and adaptive batching are enabled
[00:35] Maya: can you give an example numbers? that helps us quantify ops savings
[00:40] Jordan: sure - for the 1k token seq workload the baseline p95 was around 280ms, our p95 on the same model family with the recommended batching/kv config is ~160ms. for the 2k sequences the baseline hit ~420ms p95 and we were ~260ms p95. throughput wise tokens/sec increased from ~780 to ~1,150 under the same concurrency in our tests
[01:05] Liam: those numbers look good, are these with quantized models or full fp16?
[01:10] Jordan: good question - these runs were on q4_0 quantized variants that you gave us permission to try. we also ran fp16 baseline: fp16 p95 is slightly better than q4 for single-request low-latency but q4 gives ~20-30% cost reduction with negligible quality drop for your evals
[01:30] Priya: when you say kv cache can you clarify - is that prefix caching or per-session kv? how does it behave if we pass long context?
[01:35] Jordan: its the kv cache - we should have said K V cache in the pre-meeting note, sorry - basically prefix caching for repeated system/context. for rolling long contexts the cache helps with repeated tokens but for brand new long sequences the kv still needs to populate so p95 can spike. the adaptive batching tries to keep latency SLOs by prioritizing low-latency requests
[02:00] Samira: one notable point - your baseline provider had a higher variance on long tails; we saw a few outliers at 1.2s that were weird. our 24h runs reduced outliers but we want to validate on your traffic shape
[02:20] Maya: that outlier story is important. our SLAs for user-facing features can't tolerate >1s tails often. can we reproduce your 24h run in our VPC?
[02:27] Ethan: yes, we can run the same rig in a Private deployment or Dedicated depending on the network. For VPC we need a small test hookup - Jordan can help set up a short-term VPC peering and we can run the test with the same driver and seed traffic
[02:45] Priya: data residency - all traces we share for benchmarking need to be redacted and compliant. do you have guidance on KMS and logs?
[02:50] Jordan: we have an internal doc, but short answer - in Private you can bring your KMS/HSM, logs can be routed to your logging endpoint, and audit events are available. we'll send the SOC2 and KMS integration details after the call. note - sometimes in transcripts our product names get munged, e.g., Redwood Dedicated becomes 'Redwood Dedi' in notes but the capabilities are the same
[03:20] Liam: a couple technical clarifications - what batching sizes did you run? and how do batch windows affect p95?
[03:25] Jordan: default adaptive batching used a 30ms window with max batch of 64 tokens per shard for these tests. when we reduced window to 10ms p95 improved a bit for low-concurrency but throughput dropped. recommended is adaptive with 20-30ms window for your latency-sensitive endpoints and bump batch size for background jobs
[03:50] Maya: what about model fallbacks? if we hit capacity do you fallback to smaller quantized variant or route to other region? we need predictable degradation paths
[03:58] Samira: yes, we can set auto-fallback to a lower-accuracy quantized variant or to another compatible model in a secondary region. that way you get graceful degradation instead of hard failures
[04:15] Priya: security question - what about SAML/SSO and RBAC for the console?
[04:18] Ethan: we support SAML SSO (sometimes shows up as SAMl in some exports), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC at token/route level. will share admin guide and the roles matrix
[04:35] Jordan: back to numbers - we also measured cost-per-1M tokens: baseline roughly $X.XX (redacted in this doc), our q4 path reduces unit cost by ~25% in these runs. again we'll send the full spreadsheet; the headline is lower p95 and lower cost with q4 + kv cache + batching
[04:55] Liam: any quality regressions with q4 on our eval prompts? we ran sample sets and saw a very slight decrease in exact-match for some structured outputs
[05:00] Jordan: yes, there are edge cases where q4 affects numeric/table outputs; for those we recommended either fp16 for that route or post-processor heuristics. we can pin the route to fp16 while keeping others quantized
[05:20] Maya: ok makes sense. for the 24h run, can you include the per-route traces and the raw token-level latency histograms?
[05:26] Jordan: yep we'll upload per-route histograms and raw traces to the shared drive and flag any anomalies. we'll also include the test driver config so you can reproduce locally
[05:40] Ethan: next steps recap - Jordan will run the 24h stability run in our staging and upload traces (due 3/18), Ethan to send pricing and pilot T&Cs (due 3/19), Priya to share SOC2 and residency questions (due 3/17). schedule a pricing/exec touchpoint week of 3/22
[05:55] Maya: one last thing - we might ask for a short on-prem demo if the VPC testing looks good, can you pre-prepare an on-prem checklist?
[06:00] Samira: yes, we'll send a one-pager for Private/on-prem checklist and the top-of-stack requirements
[06:10] Ethan: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and the links. talk soon
